title: Infra: GPU Fleet, Capacity & CI/CD IaC Playbook
author: Avery Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference engineering guidance for GPU fleet design, capacity planning, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD build pipelines, and operational runbooks. It is intended for infra, platform, SRE, and serving-runtime engineers who operate or modify GPU-backed inference capacity.

Scope:
- GPU fleets (hosted & Dedicated) on AWS and GCP
- Terraform/IaC modules for GPU node pools, VPC networking, IAM, and autoscaling
- CI/CD for infra modules and AMI/container bake pipelines
- Runbooks for capacity events, node maintenance, and incident triage

Ownership and Contacts:
- Primary owner: infra-engineering (pager: #infra-oncall)
- Secondary owner: eng-sre (pager: #sre-oncall)
- Module maintainers: infra-iac-team (owners listed in module README)
- Emergency contact: oncall manager (rotate in runbook)

Terminology:
- GPU node pool: a set of instances with identical GPU/CPU/memory used by a workload (e.g., r-infer-prod-nvidia-a100-pool)
- Capacity unit: 1 A100-40GB equivalent (used for normalized capacity planning)
- Headroom: reserved spare capacity for load spikes (target 15% for production)
- Cold/Hot scaling: scheduled scale vs autoscaling based on metrics

Architecture overview (high level):
- Serving runtime runs on GPU node pools behind the inference autoscaler service.
- Requests enter via API Gateway -> Load balancer -> Router (policy-based routing) -> GPU pool.
- Key infra services: fleet-manager, autoscaler, capacity-metrics (Prometheus), rollout-controller.

Capacity planning and SLOs:
- SLOs: 99.9% cluster-level availability for inference-serving (measured per-region).
- Latency target: p99 <= 300ms for short-generation paths (<= 256 tokens); p95 <= 150ms.
- Buffer policy: maintain minimum headroom >= max(15% of committed capacity, capacity for 20 concurrent peak in-flight requests).
- Normalization: convert all GPU SKUs to 'A100-40GB equivalents' using performance table (see appendix).
- Monthly capacity review checklist:
  1) Compare actual 95th percentile concurrent tokens/sec to committed capacity.
  2) Run cost vs performance simulation in 'capacity-planner' notebook.
  3) Adjust reserved pool sizes and node types.

Autoscaling and thresholds (recommended defaults):
- Metric: running_inflight_requests_per_pool (1m average) and queue_length (5m).
- Scale-up: > 70% utilization for 3 consecutive 1m windows OR queue_length > 50 for 2m.
- Scale-down: < 40% utilization for 10m and queue_length == 0.
- Surge cooldown: 180s after scale-up to allow KV cache warmup; avoid thrash.

Terraform / IaC module conventions:
- Module naming: modules/gpu-node-pool, modules/vpc-network, modules/iam-roles, modules/instance-image-bake.
- Module inputs: region, environment, instance_type, desired_capacity, min_capacity, max_capacity, gpu_family_tag, subnet_ids, iam_role_arn.
- Module outputs: autoscaling_group_id, instance_profile_arn, node_pool_tag.
- Example usage (HCL):

```hcl
module "gpu_node_pool" {
  source          = "git::ssh://git@github.com:redwood/infra-iac.git//modules/gpu-node-pool"
  region          = "us-west-2"
  environment     = "prod"
  instance_type   = "p4d.24xlarge"
  desired_capacity = 6
  min_capacity    = 2
  max_capacity    = 30
  subnet_ids      = var.subnet_ids
  iam_role_arn    = module.iam.gpu_node_role_arn
}
```

- Approved instance families (2026): A100, A40, H100, L4 for inference. Prefer H100/A100 for high throughput; A40 and L4 for lower-cost/embedding workloads.
- Image baking: use Packer to bake a minimal inference AMI (or container image) with pinned CUDA/CuDNN, Triton/runtime, and our kernel patches. Tag AMIs with immutable version: redwood-infer-ami-YYYYMMDD-<git-sha>.

CI/CD and build pipelines:
- Repo layout: infra-iac/ (modules + env overlays), infra-bakes/ (packer + images), infra-pipelines/ (CI templates).
- Pipeline stages for IaC modules: lint (tflint, tfsec), unit plan (terragrunt/terraform validate + plan against ephemeral workspace), policy check (OPA/Conftest), PR review, integration test (apply to sandbox account), promote to env.
- Gate: All plan diffs that change autoscaling or node counts must be approved by infra-sre and cost-ops reviewers.
- Bake pipeline: trigger on main branch tags; outputs AMI/container digest to artifact registry and updates module image_version input via PR to infra-iac.
- Example GitHub Actions snippet (simplified):

```yaml
name: IaC Plan
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v1
      - name: Run tflint
      - name: Terraform init/plan
        run: terraform init && terraform plan -out=tfplan.binary
      - name: Upload plan artifact

```

Secrets & cross-account access:
- Use AWS IAM roles with external_id for cross-account deploys (sandbox -> prod).
- Store short-lived deploy credentials in Vault and use OIDC where possible.

Network & cloud accounts guidance:
- VPC design: dedicated inference VPC per region with private subnets for GPU pools, NAT for outbound, and restricted egress ACLs for model artifacts.
- DNS: internal service discovery via Route53 private hosted zones; ensure split-horizon DNS for staging vs prod.
- Peering and Transit: Use Transit Gateway for cross-account traffic where low-latency is required. For Dedicated customers, use VPC peering or Transit Gateway attachments as per contract.
- Network Sizing: plan for 25 Gbps per host for A100/H100 classes; verify ENI/ENA limits and SR-IOV settings.

Operational runbooks (actions & playbooks):
- Runbook: Add capacity during sustained high utilization
  1) Confirm metric anomaly: check capacity-metrics dashboard (last 1h) and increase request queue length.
  2) Open channel #infra-ops with summary and link to dashboards.
  3) If autoscaler is healthy, increase desired_capacity for affected pool via terraform env overlay and trigger apply.
  4) If autoscaler not responding, scale the ASG/instance group directly (CLI):

```bash
# AWS example: increase desired capacity
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name r-infer-prod-a100-pool --desired-capacity 12 --region us-west-2
```

  5) After nodes join, warm caches: run rolling warmup job: curl -s "http://router.internal/warm?pool=a100&targets=all"
  6) Monitor latency (p95/p99) and queue_length for 30m.

- Runbook: Replace degraded GPU instances
  1) Identify failing instance via instance status and node labels.
  2) Cordon node (k8s) or mark instance drained in service: mark unschedulable, drain connections, wait for in-flight requests to finish (max wait 300s).
  3) Remove instance from pool and create replacement via ASG or instance template.
  4) If hardware fault, tag instance with maintenance reason and file ticket with cloud provider.

- Incident triage checklist for capacity saturation:
  1) Check autoscaler logs and RL metrics.
  2) Confirm there are no runaway prompts (rate-limiter events).
  3) If model regression increases latency per token, rollback model rollout policy to previous stable variant.
  4) If demand surge, activate emergency scale-up policy and notify sales/CS per SLA.

Change & rollout process for pool changes:
- Canary strategy: change min_capacity in sandbox -> smoke tests -> promote to staging -> canary in prod with 10% traffic for 30m -> full rollout.
- Rollback criteria: p99 latency > 2x baseline or error rate > 1% for 10m.

Verification and testing:
- Unit tests: module-level tests using terraform-compliance and kitchen-terraform.
- Integration tests: spin up 2-node pool in sandbox, run synthetic load (wrk/locust) with generation profiles.
- Bake validation: run inference smoke tests against baked image (model load, KV cache, sample prompt).

Metrics and dashboards (recommended):
- Core metrics: instance_gpu_utilization, inflight_requests, queue_length, avg_tokens_per_request, request_error_rate.
- Alert thresholds: queue_length > 50 for 5m (P2), p99 latency > 3x baseline for 5m (P1).

Appendix:
- Example capacity calculation: 1 A100-40GB equiv handles ~200 concurrent short-generation requests at target latency. So for p95=1000 concurrent requests, require 1000/200 = 5 capacity units, add 15% headroom -> 6 units. Map to nodes: if node = 4 A100 equiv -> desired_capacity = ceil(6/4) = 2 nodes.

- Sample Terraform variable table (text):
  - region: string
  - environment: [dev|staging|prod]
  - instance_type: string
  - desired_capacity: number
  - min_capacity: number
  - max_capacity: number
  - subnet_ids: list(string)
  - iam_role_arn: string

- Common CLI snippets:
```bash
# Check autoscaler status
curl -s http://autoscaler.internal/health | jq .
# Force terraform plan for prod overlay
terragrunt plan --terragrunt-working-dir env/prod/gpu-pool
```
